profile.summary: SPACE is a DNA model that learns sequence representations by supervised training rather than by masked or next-token prediction. It is trained to predict thousands of genomic profiles, such as chromatin accessibility, transcription factor binding, histone marks and CAGE, from long human and mouse DNA sequences. Its encoder can then be fine-tuned or used as a feature extractor for other DNA tasks, and the full model predicts the profiles themselves.
profile.summary_source_locator: Paper: Abstract; 4.1 Pre-training; README: Try the Genomic Profile Prediction, Downstream Tasks

summary_quotes.text: Here, we demonstrate that supervised training for genomic profile prediction serves as a more effective alternative to pure sequence pre-training.

containing DNA sequences and corresponding genomic profiles for human and mouse genomes. Both species shared four conserved profile types: chromatin accessibility (DNase/ATAC-seq), transcription factor binding (TF ChIP-seq), histone modifications (Histone ChIP-seq), and transcriptional activity (CAGE).
We provide code for genomic profile prediction in both `test_Enformer.ipynb` and `test_SPACE.ipynb`.
We provide code for reproducing downstream tasks in the folder `experiments/`.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: SPACE (Species-Profile Adaptive Collaborative Experts) keeps the Enformer setup of predicting genomic profiles from DNA, and adds two Mixture of Experts (MoE) parts. A species-aware encoder adds a trainable species embedding and routes each input sparsely across experts, so it can learn both species-specific and shared features. A profile-grouped enhancement decoder uses gated experts to model dependencies between profile types before the human and mouse output heads. The implementation is based on Enformer-Pytorch and Mod-Squad. In the released configuration the input is 131,072 bp, the model width is 1536 with 11 layers and 8 attention heads, the species MoE has 4 experts and the profile MoE has 8, and topk is set to 3.
sections.source_locator: Paper: Introduction; 3 Method; README: Acknowledgments; config.json

quotes.text: which consists of two key components: (1) a species-aware encoder module and (2) a profile-grouped enhancement decoder module, both built upon Mixture of Experts (MoE).

The species-aware encoder employs sparse routing to dynamically balance species-specific and shared biological features, while the profile-grouped enhancement decoder uses dual-gated expert weighted aggregation to capture the intricate dependencies between different genomic profiles.
Our implementation is based on [Enformer-Pytorch](https://github.com/lucidrains/enformer-pytorch) and [Mod-Squad](https://github.com/UMass-Embodied-AGI/Mod-Squad).

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: The README names one pretrained checkpoint, yangyz1230/space on Hugging Face, which appears to be the paper's SPACE (large). Smaller variants in the paper (hidden size 768) were built only for ablation studies, and the README names none of them. The training data are the Enformer human and mouse sets, which the authors converted from the Basenji TensorFlow files to H5 and published as the Hugging Face dataset yangyz1230/space. A result should name the checkpoint revision; this page read revision 63c9f501.
sections.source_locator: README: Pre-trained Model, Dataset; Paper: Appendix H; Hugging Face API response

quotes.text: We have uploaded our model config and weights to 🤗 Hugging Face Hub at: https://huggingface.co/yangyz1230/space.

The SPACE (large) configuration represents our primary model with complete architectural components for comparative analysis, while the other variants correspond to reduced-scale models specifically designed for ablation studies.
We have converted the data to H5 format and made it freely available for download on 🤗 Hugging Face: https://huggingface.co/datasets/yangyz1230/space.

sections.title: Evaluation in the paper
sections.body: The authors fine-tuned the encoder on the Nucleotide Transformer downstream tasks, where they report the best result on 11 of 18 tasks, including against the 2.5B-parameter NT-Multispecies model, and they compare with Enformer on the GUE benchmark. With frozen embeddings on the BEND benchmark they report strong results on chromatin accessibility, histone modification and CpG methylation, but limited effectiveness on the two variant effect tasks. These are the authors' own results.

quotes.text: our model achieves SOTA performance on 11 out of 18 prediction tasks
Comparison Results with Enformer on the GUE Benchmark.
We observe that SPACE achieves SOTA performance on chromatin accessibility, histone modification, and CpG methylation tasks
However, on the two variant effects tasks, SPACE shows limited effectiveness, similar to most DFMs.

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: Supervised DNA foundation model: a genomic profile predictor whose learned representations are reused for downstream DNA tasks.

quotes.text: establishing that DNA models trained with supervised genomic profiles serve as powerful DNA representation learners

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Enformer-style model (architecture name MultiSpeciesEnformer) with a species-aware MoE encoder and a profile-grouped MoE decoder: width 1536, 11 layers, 8 heads, 7 downsampling steps, 4 species experts and 8 profile experts, topk 3.

quotes.text: both built upon Mixture of Experts (MoE)

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: A DNA sequence of 131,072 bp from human or mouse, with the species identified so the species embedding can be applied.
facts.source_locator: config.json; Paper: Appendix B Table 5; 3 Method

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: Predicted genomic profile tracks over 896 output bins: 5313 tracks for human and 1643 for mouse. The encoder's intermediate representations serve as DNA embeddings for fine-tuning or as frozen features.
facts.source_locator: config.json: output_heads, target_length; Paper: Appendix E

quotes.text: directly using frozen SPACE embeddings for downstream tasks

facts.label: Parameters
facts.value: 588M, sparsely activated (588.75M in the paper's parameter table) for the released SPACE (large) model.

quotes.text: Model Parameter Counts of SPACE and its ablation variants

facts.label: Training data
facts.value: The Enformer human and mouse training set: DNA sequences paired with genomic profiles in four classes (DNase/ATAC-seq, TF ChIP-seq, histone ChIP-seq, CAGE). Batches were balanced between the two species.

quotes.text: Our model was pretrained on the same dataset as Enformer
we implemented balanced batch sampling through randomized minority-class augmentation, ensuring equal representation of both species in every batch

run_guide.summary: Get the SPACE code at a pinned commit, build its conda environment and load the pretrained SPACE model from Hugging Face.
prerequisites: conda. The environment file pins python 3.8.19, pytorch 2.1.1 built for CUDA 12.1, and transformers 4.45.2, so an NVIDIA GPU with CUDA 12.1 support is expected. GPU memory needs are not stated.
The code is MIT licensed. No licence is stated for the weights; the Hugging Face repository is not gated.

steps.title: Get the code at the pinned commit
steps.shell:
git clone https://github.com/ZhuJiwei111/SPACE
cd SPACE
git checkout --detach 4cdba18b80f948410623acee4b27a988ae7ddace
steps.explanation: The clone and cd lines are from the model card. The checkout line is added to pin the commit this page was written from.

steps.title: Create the environment
steps.shell:
conda env create -f environment.yml
conda activate space
steps.explanation: Builds and activates the conda environment that holds the repository's dependencies.

steps.title: Load the pretrained model
steps.shell:
python - <<'PY'
from model.modeling_space import Space
model_name_or_path = "yangyz1230/space"
model = Space.from_pretrained(model_name_or_path)
PY
steps.explanation: The README snippet wrapped in a shell heredoc, run from the repository root so that the model package is importable. It downloads the config and weights from Hugging Face.
steps.source_locator: README: Pre-trained Model; model card: Usage

outputs: A loaded SPACE model in memory. The snippet prints nothing; profile prediction examples are in the notebooks test_SPACE.ipynb and test_Enformer.ipynb, which were not read.

notes: Code (ZhuJiwei111/SPACE) and weights (yangyz1230/space) have different owners; the README links to the weights and the model card links to the code, and both name the same ICML 2025 paper, so both are treated as official. The weights licence is not stated. The GENEB leaderboard lists 'space' with params 588750000, which matches the paper's 588.75M.
